substituting an Mg atom with a Gd atom leads to a large negative misﬁt( /C0 0.125) and compression strain [29]. This stress will roughen the slip plane and resist the dislocation movement and strengthen the material.
The β′ plate shaped phase which grows on the prismatic plane of the Mg matrix in dense triangular arrangement reported to be the most effective barrier to dislocation glide [28].
Grain boundary strengthening is another reason for the higher mechanical properties of the Mg –12Gd–3Y–0.5Zr alloy.
